title: Glassy carbon electrode modified with Fe3O4/CuS/PANI/RGO nanostructure for efficient electrochemical sensing of mangiferin
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: A Fe3O4/CuS/PANI/RGO nanostructure was created for this investigation. Several methods were used to examine the structure and morphology of the Fe3O4/CuS/PANI/RGO nanostructure, and then as a working electrode for the voltammetric detection of mangiferin (MANG), a glassy carbon electrode (GCE) modified with a manufactured nanostructure (Fe3O4/CuS/PANI/RGO/GCE) was used. The Fe3O4/CuS/PANI/RGO/GCE showed superior electro-catalytic activity for MANG oxidation as compared to unmodified GCE. The limit of detection (LOD) is 0.5±0.02 μM, and under ideal circumstances, the oxidation peak currents of MANG show a linear relationship with its concentration in the range of 1.0–250.0 μM. Lastly, MANG analysis was used to confirm the constructed sensor's applicability in real samples, yielding outstanding results (recovery 98.0–104.3%, and relative standard deviation (RSD) < 3.4%).

title: Modified voltammetric sensors for measurement of methyl parathion
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: Population growth of humans leads to expansion of industrial agriculture in which pesticides are an essential component. These chemicals allow the destruction of harmful factors such as weeds, insects, and microbes; that not only damage the health value of foods, but also cause unpleasant effects on human beings. Hence, detection, and quantification of pesticides are vital issues concerning human beings’ health. Since the development of numerous analytical chemical methods for the determination of these organic compounds, electrochemical techniques, considering their sensitivity, selectivity, low cost, and environmental friendliness have received wide interest recently. This paper reviews the research papers that concern the construction and performance of modified electrochemical voltammetric sensors to determine and quantify pesticides.

title: Molecular dynamics simulation and conformational stability analysis of HPV-16 E6 oncoprotein–ligand complexes: cilostazol as a promising stable candidate
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV-16) is a primary driver of cervical cancer and several other malignancies. The viral E6 oncoprotein promotes oncogenesis by mediating the degradation of the tumor suppressor p53. Therefore, compounds capable of maintaining stable interactions with E6 may provide a rational basis for antiviral and anticancer drug development. In this study, the dynamic stability of five selected ligands (axitinib, cabozantinib, tivozanib, deflazacort, and cilostazol) in complex with HPV-16 E6 was evaluated through 300-ns all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using GROMACS 2022.4, the CHARMM36 force field, and the TIP3P water model. Structural stability, flexibility, compactness, and interaction persistence were assessed using RMSD, RMSF, hydrogen bonding, radius of gyration (Rg), protein–ligand distance, contact number, and solvent-accessible surface area (SASA) analyses. Among the five complexes, the cilostazol–E6 system exhibited the most favorable overall dynamic stability profile throughout the 300-ns simulation. It maintained 6–10 persistent hydrogen bonds, a stable radius of gyration (~1.70 nm), a consistent protein–ligand distance (~0.18 nm), and a protein–ligand contact profile that increased from approximately 800–1200 contacts during the early stage to 1500–2000 contacts during the later phase of the simulation, along with an average SASA of approximately 97 nm², collectively reflecting sustained structural integrity and interaction persistence. In comparison, the other ligands (axitinib, cabozantinib, tivozanib, and deflazacort) generally exhibited less favorable dynamic behavior across the evaluated molecular dynamics parameters, indicating lower overall complex stability. These findings demonstrate that cilostazol forms a more stable complex with HPV-16 E6 than the other tested compounds and represents a promising candidate for further experimental investigation as a potential E6-targeted antiviral and anticancer agent.

title: Nanomedicine-induced transcriptomic biomarkers in gastrointestinal cancers
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: Gastrointestinal cancers (GIC) are leading causes of cancer mortality with limited therapeutic options. Nanomedicine offers targeted delivery, reduced toxicity, and enhanced efficacy in GIC; however, the molecular response to these therapies, particularly nanoparticle therapy, remains unclear. This study analyzed three RNA-Seq datasets representing three therapeutic modalities: Ramucirumab (an anti-VEGFR2 monoclonal antibody) in gastric cancer; Anti-miR-17 (an anti-miRNA oligonucleotide) in hepatocellular carcinoma; and β-cyclodextrin-EDTA-Fe₃O₄ nanoparticles (CPT-CEF) in colorectal cancer. Among these, only CPT-CEF represents a nanoparticle-based nanomedicine. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified via DESeq2 (|log₂FC|≥1, adj.P≤0.05), followed by Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analysis. Treatment with these modalities, particularly the CPT-CEF nanoparticle formulation, significantly modulated metabolic pathways (carbon metabolism, purine/pyrimidine metabolism, and oxidative phosphorylation), DNA replication, and ribosome biogenesis. A core set of genes (MCM2, MCM5, MCM7, POLA2, FEN1, RNASEH2A, POLD1, POLD2, RNASEH1, EPHX2, RRM2, CCNA2, PLK1, CHEK1, and TOP2A) was consistently dysregulated in GIC and reversed upon treatment. These genes regulate cell cycle progression, DNA repair, and metabolic reprogramming, serving as promising biomarkers for therapy efficacy, particularly for nanoparticle-based treatment, and potential targets for nanocarrier-based delivery. The findings provide a molecular rationale for smart nanotherapeutics, aligning with nanomaterials and medicinal chemistry. This in silico strategy offers a cost-effective approach to identify novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets, accelerating personalized therapy, including nanomedicine, for GIC.

title: A modified pencil electrode based on binary transition-metal sulfide nanoparticles for sensitive detection of the herbicide Diuron
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: The development of sensitive analytical methods with extremely low detection limits has consistently remained a critical challenge in the control and monitoring of herbicide residues in agricultural food products. In this regard, transition metal sulfide nanostructures can make a significant contribution to the development of effective electrochemical sensors to address this challenge. Needle-shaped CuₓBi₂₋ₓS₃ nanoparticles were employed as an effective electrocatalyst for the sensitive determination of trace amounts of the herbicide Diuron using a graphite pencil based electrochemical sensor. The proposed sensor was successfully applied for the determination of Diuron over a concentration range of 40 to 900 µg/L, with a limit of detection of 17 µg/L and a sensitivity of 0.251 µA·L·µg⁻¹, without any significant interference from coexisting species. Differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) was utilized as the analytical method, and the structure of the synthesized nanocomposite was confirmed by X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX).

title: Biochemistry techniques in diabetes disease studies
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a prevalent metabolic disease that causes many complications when it is poorly managed in terms of blood glucose control. Diagnosing diabetes and its complications require accurate measuring of biochemical and molecular markers of diseases. Recently, several biochemical approaches have been developed to identify proteins, antibodies, cytokines, hormones, and other disease markers in biological samples. The present review provides a brief description of major biochemical approaches employed for investigating diabetes with special attention paid to four approaches emphasized in this review, namely enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), Luminex, single-molecule array (SiMoA), and agglutination-PCR (ADAP). Overall, the discussed biochemical approaches offer complementary information regarding development of diabetes and its complications. Increased sensitivity, ability for multiplexing, and early biomarker detection of discussed biochemical approaches may advance the field of diabetes research. Studies included in the present paper are devoted to different types of research on diabetes but all of them use one of the discussed biochemical approaches as the detection method.

title: Synthesis and investigation of structural and magnetic properties of Fe₂O₃/Fe₃O₄/MWCNT ternary nanocomposite: Application for the detection of the medicine drug epinine
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: The main objective of this project is to develop a new electrochemical sensor which detects epinephrine. Researchers synthesized the FeO₃/FeO₄/MWCNT ternary nanocomposite through a simple process which they used multiple microscopic and spectroscopic methods to determine its crystallinity and content and shape. The researchers studied how the fabricated nanocomposite performed in electrochemical tests which involved morphine detection after they deposited the material onto a screen-printed graphite electrode (SPGE). The SPGE developed through nanocomposite modification showed better electrocatalytic performance than the unmodified electrode when testing for epinine oxidation. The researchers examined the current sensor (Fe₂O₃/Fe₃O₄/MWCNT/SPE) using differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) under controlled laboratory conditions. The research results showed a linear dynamic range which extended from 1.0 to 200.0 µM together with a limit of detection (LOD) which reached 0.4 µM. The predicted sensitivity was 0.1894 µA/ µM. Researchers used the Fe₃O₃/Fe₃O₄/MWCNT for voltammetric measurements of epinine in urine samples which resulted in recovery rates of approximately 100% for all tested samples.

title: Synergistic investigation of hexagonal α-MnTe phase synthesized via electrochemical deposition technique for photovoltaic application
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: Manganese telluride (MnTe) is another promising p-type semiconductor for photovoltaic (PV) systems, noted for its high absorption coefficient and tunable band gaps. MnTe thin films in this paper, was deposited on the fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) substrate through an electrochemical deposition process. X-ray diffraction (XRD) was used to analyze the structure and supported the standard lattice planes with the hexagonal α-MnTe phase with diffraction peaks of between 25.3o and 75.3o. Morphology on the surface indicated that the early deposition produced single islands, which caused a rough surface. Nevertheless, with the deposition duration increased to 40 seconds, the grain coalescence, and a more homogeneous film is formed. Additional optimization of the deposition time of 50 seconds however increased the thickness of the film and the grain size and improved the maximum absorbance within the UV-visible and near-infrared (NIR) spectra. This expansion also increased the light-trapping ability, which is essential in enhancing high density of current during short circuit. Direct band gap is 1.79 eV, and such electrodeposited MnTe films present a high potential in top-cell absorber in tandem solar cell arrangements on a substrate with lower band gaps.

title: Measurement of butylated hydroxyanisol in food samples using carbon electrode modified with Zn-metal organic framework nanostructures
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: Butylated hydroxyanisole (BHA) functions as a potent chemical antioxidant which protects food and food packaging materials and animal feed and cosmetics and pharmaceutical products and rubber and petroleum products. For the sensitive detection of BHA, a Zn-metal organic framework nanostructure (Zn-MOF) is used to modify a screen-printed graphite electrode (SPE). The oxidation process of BHA on the modified SPE was significantly electrocatalyzed by the synergistic impact of Zn-MOF. With a linear concentration range of 0.6–190.0 μM, a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.2 μM, and a high sensitivity of 0.0804 μA/μM, BHA was quantitatively detected. For the detection of BHA, the Zn-MOF/SPE sensor showed high stability, repeatability, and reproducibility. Furthermore, the evaluation of the interference effect of several species on BHA detection showed that the sensor's design has high selectivity for BHA. With recoveries ranging from 96.1 to 103.2% and a relative standard deviation (RSD) of 3.6%, the Zn-MOF/SPE sensor was effectively utilized to determine BHA in actual samples.

title: Plant-mediated green synthesis and characterization of zinc oxide nanoparticle for enhanced antimicrobial activities against Escherichia coli
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: Medicinal plants have long been a crucial component of traditional medicine, retaining their importance in human health management for centuries. These plants act as a reservoir of bioactive compounds, which are known to possess antimicrobial properties. Despite the availability of various antimicrobial agents, concerns regarding antibiotic resistance remain prevalent. Several strategies are employed to address this issue. In this study, zinc oxide nanoparticles synthesized from Iccacina oliviformis were prepared using an eco-friendly precipitation method. The antimicrobial activities of both the aqueous extract and the synthesized nanoparticles were assessed using minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) methods. Characterization of the prepared zinc oxide nanoparticles was performed using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Phytochemical analysis identified several constituents, including alkaloids, tannins, saponins, flavonoids, terpenoids, and anthraquinones. The ZnO NPs synthesized from Iccacina oliviformis demonstrated stronger antimicrobial activity, with an MIC of 0.98 µg/mL, compared to 7.8 µg/mL for the aqueous extract of Iccacina oliviformis root tuber alone. FTIR analysis revealed the presence of alcohols, carbonyls, alkenes, and nitro-compounds, phenols, functional groups originating from O-H, C=O, C–C, N=O, and C-H. The XRD analysis indicated a hexagonal wurtzite phase of ZnO, while SEM images displayed nano-sized structures characterized by agglomeration and high surface roughness. The formation of ZnO nanoparticles was clearly observed in this study, and antimicrobial assays confirmed that the synthesized ZnO nanoparticles exhibited inhibitory effects against Escherichia coli. Further research is needed to investigate the potential toxicities associated with the synthesized nanoparticles.

title: Electrochemical sensor based on modified carbon paste electrode for isoniazid detection
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: Isoniazid (ISD) is a commonly prescribed antibiotic medication used to treat tuberculosis. To detect isoniazid (ISD), a carbon paste electrode (ZnFe2O4/CPE) was modified using ZnFe2O4 nanostructures. Analysis revealed that ISD electro-oxidation had a remarkable catalytic activity, leading to a significant peak potential decrease (~130 mV) for ISD. The electrochemical characteristics of the modified electrode for the ISD detection were characterized using chronoamperometry, differential pulse voltammetry (DPV), linear sweep voltammogram (LSV), and cyclic voltammetry (CV). The peak current of oxidation and the different levels of ISD (0.1–300.0 µM) showed a linear relationship under ideal conditions, with a narrow detection limit of 0.04±0.001 µM. By measuring the ISD in tablets and urine specimens, the as-developed sensor's applicability was verified with respectable recoveries.

title: A novel nano complex of Zn (II) with turmeric: Synthesis, characterization, spectroscopic methods, and interaction with FS-DNA
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: This study examined a zinc (II) ion nano-complex with curcumin (turmeric) ligand. X-ray scattering, scanning electron microscopy, and UV-Vis and Fourier infrared spectroscopies were used to identify the nanoparticles after they were generated using the ultrasonic probe approach. The scanning electron microscope's images demonstrated the particles' consistent shape. The size of the particles was less than 100 nm, according to calculations based on the model, which is evidence that nanoparticles were generated. Lastly, fluorescence, UV-Vis, and gel electrophoresis techniques were used to study the interaction of nanoparticle (a) with fish salmon DNA (FS-DNA). These interactions were also used to derive the thermodynamic values ΔH°, ΔS°, and ΔG°. The results demonstrated how hydrogen bonds and van der Waals forces contribute to the groove binding form of interaction between the DNA and the nano-complex (a). The finding that larger concentrations of the complex had no effect on the viscosity of the DNA was particularly intriguing since it suggests that the binding interaction did not significantly disrupt the helical structure of the DNA. Circular dichroism (CD) spectra revealed that the interaction with the nano-complex significantly altered the DNA structure (a). This discovery highlights the necessity of using multiple analytical tools to successfully distinguish between metal-DNA interactions and shows how complicatedly they subtly affect DNA structure.

title: Electrochemical determination of medicinal drug gliclazide using carbon paste electrode modified with Fe3O4/GO nanocomposites
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: This study presents the solvothermal synthesis of a FeO₄@CuO core-shell nanostructure. The synthesized materials were extensively characterized to determine their chemical bonding, element composition, and macro, and microstructure. To characterize the nanostructures, advanced analytical characterization methods were used, including Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray Diffraction (XRD), Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM), and Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FE-SEM/EDX). The successful synthesis of the core-shell structure was unequivocally confirmed through these characterization techniques, which also provided insight into the morphology of the synthesized nanostructures along with structural support. Afterward, an electrochemical sensor based on a modified carbon paste electrode, using FeO₄@CuO core-shell nanostructure, was developed for detecting gliclazide. The modified electrode showed effective behavior in gliclazide electrocatalysis, an experimental sensor created using Fe3O4/GO/CPE compared to bare CPE shows a significant decrease in peak potentials and an increase in sensor sensitivities. The sensor was used to detect gliclazide using differential pulse voltammetry. A detection limit of 0.03 µM (S/N=3) was identified, and a linear correspondence of response currents and gliclazide concentrations was found over the broader concentration range of 1.0-700.0 µM. The study findings suggest that Fe3O4/GO/CPE presents an effective voltametric sensor for future analyses. The sensors showed the ability to effectively detect gliclazide in real samples with high sensitivity.

title: Application of metal-organic framework-based nanocomposites as drug delivery systems for doxorubicin anticancer drug
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX), a prominent chemotherapeutic agent from the anthracycline class, is extensively utilized in the management of diverse malignancies, including cervical carcinoma, osteosarcoma, and breast cancer. A major limitation of DOX is its lack of target specificity, leading to significant damage to healthy cells and resulting in a range of adverse side effects. A drug delivery system (DDS) is designed to transport pharmaceutical agents in a controlled and sustained manner, specifically to targeted sites within the body. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) possess a suite of advantageous characteristics for drug delivery, including high design flexibility, precisely defined porosity, stimuli-responsive behavior, an exceptionally large surface area, and tunable morphology. To date, numerous MOF structures have been extensively investigated and employed as nanocarriers. Their significant appeal in the realm of drug delivery stems from their favorable biocompatibility and exceptional capacity for high drug loading. MOFs, particularly when integrated with complementary materials, have been widely explored as innovative carrier platforms for the delivery of DOX. DDSs function by releasing their active pharmaceutical ingredients in a manner designed to achieve a specific and optimal therapeutic outcome. MOFs serve as a versatile foundational platform for drug delivery, often integrated into nanocomposite materials such as MOF-polymer nanocomposites, MOF-metal oxide nanocomposites, and MOF-graphene oxide nanocomposites. Herein, a summary of MOF nanocomposite-based DDSs for the delivery of DOX is provided over the last eight years.

title: Electrochemical detection of methionine using zeolitic imidazolate framework, cobalt ferrite, ionic liquid, and ferrocene monocaroxylic acid modified carbon paste electrode
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: Methionine is a vitamin soluble in water which is found in numerous natural species. Human body eventually runs into problems with the absence of methionine, thus a method that is easy and sensitive for detecting methionine is desired. A new electrode that has been chemically modified was meant for methionine measurement in real samples using zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF-67), cobalt ferrite (CoFe2O4), ionic liquid (IL), and Ferrocene monocaroxylic acid (FMC) modified carbon paste electrode (CPE). ZIF-67@CoFe2O4/IL/FMC/CPE was analyzed through scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The parameters of pH and scan rate (ν) were studied by cyclic voltammetry, and the optimized values were selected. The electrochemical parameters, such as diffusion coefficient of methionine (DMethionine), electrode surface area (A), and electron transfer coefficient (α) were determined. For quantitative computations, the accuracy of square wave voltammetry was utilized. A two-linear relation was discovered between anodic peak current (ipa) and methionine concentration (CMethionine) in the 0.1-10.0 µM and 10.0-600.0 µM1 ranges; the limit of detection (LOD) was thus set at 0.03 µM, which is on par with prior research. A novel, simple, quick, and selective sensor was examined to determine methionine in real samples.

title: Development of an electrochemical sensor based on ferrocene dicarboxylic acid/Ce-doped SnO2 nanosheets-modified carbon paste electrode for epinine detection
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: A carbon paste electrode (CPE) that was modified with ferrocene dicarboxylic acid (FDC) and Ce-doped SnO2 nanosheets (Ce-doped SnO2 NSs) was created for the purpose of efficient epinine detection. Various analytical methods such as field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) were applied to determine the chemical composition and surface morphology of the prepared Ce-doped SnO2nanosheets. Furthermore, the modified electrodes (FDC/Ce-doped SnO2 NSs/CPE) were tested in a pH range of 2 to 9 for their respective activities towards epinine detection. The electrochemical technique was applied for the determination of the range and limit of detection. The modified electrode exhibited a linear detection range of 0.1-300.0 µM. Moreover, the LODs for low and high doses were equal to 0.03±0.001 µM, respectively. Among the kinetic properties of epinine in different media, diffusion and transport coefficients were studied. Finally, the modified electrode was tested for its activity on an actual sample.

title: Emerging role of endophytic fungi in nano-medicine: A review
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: Medicinal plants are natural sources of therapeutic compounds and play crucial roles in drug discovery. The analysis of phytochemicals, both in terms of quality and quantity, plays a pivotal role in defining a plant's nutritional, pharmaceutical, and biological characteristics. In addition to secondary metabolites, certain microorganisms, referred to as endophytes, have co-evolved with their host plants and produce metabolites similar to those of the host plant, which are of therapeutic value. Among eukaryotic organisms, fungi are a significant group known for their capacity to produce diverse compounds, some of which have direct applications as medicines or in synthetic processes. Myco-nanobiotechnology is a rapidly growing research field that has significantly contributed to the development of novel opportunities and applications in nanomedicine. This breakthrough provides a new approach for producing effective compounds with effects similar to those of natural medicines extracted from plants. This review aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the exciting field of endophytic fungi-mediated synthesis of nanoparticles (NPs) and their pharmacological applications. By addressing the challenges and future perspectives, this review will contribute to the advancement of nanotechnology in medicine and pave the way for innovative therapeutic interventions.

title: Recent progress in graphitic carbon nitride-based systems for photocatalytic antibiotics degradation: A review
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: The widespread use of antibiotics in both human healthcare and animal husbandry has led to their persistent presence in various aquatic ecosystems. The accelerating spread of antimicrobial resistance is closely linked to an emerging worldwide health emergency, where a rising number of infectious illnesses are no longer responsive to standard treatment regimens. In response, a variety of approaches have recently been developed to remediate antibiotic contamination. In this context, photodegradation offers a highly promising method for tackling this escalating problem, enabling the complete degradation of antibiotics into harmless byproducts. This technology represents a promising, environmentally safe, and cost-effective approach for the removal of various antibiotics. Graphitic carbon nitride (g-C₃N₄) is widely regarded as a highly promising material for photocatalysis, particularly in applications like environmental cleanup through the removal of organic pollutants. g-C₃N₄-based photocatalysts responsive to visible or sunlight have been extensively investigated for antibiotic breakdown, benefiting from their strong chemical and thermal stability, adjustable photophysical characteristics, and straightforward synthesis routes. This review focuses on the use of diverse g-C₃N₄-based photocatalysts in degrading a range of antibiotics—including sulfonamides, tetracyclines, quinolones, and others—with particular emphasis on their degradation efficiency under varying reaction parameters such as light sources and reaction conditions.

title: Voltammetric determination of catechol in food ingredients using screen printed electrode modified with Fe3O4 nanoparticles
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: CTC serves as an industrial precursor which manufacturers use to create various products including flavors, pesticides, scents, plastics, herbicides, dyes, tanning agents, rubber, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, preservatives, antioxidants, lubricating oils, and stabilizer materials. Fe3O4 nanoparticles were created here utilizing a straightforward method and are employed as a voltammetric sensing platform. Fe3O4 nanoparticles provide better sensor performance. The sensor was created by applying a suspension of Fe3O4 nanoparticles to a screen-printed carbon electrode (Fe3O4/SPCE) using a simple drop-casting technique. The catechol (CTC) was then measured using a differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) technique using the Fe3O4/SPCE sensor. The Fe3O4 nanoparticles/SPCE sensor showed a high sensitivity of 0.117 µA/µM and a linear response to CTC throughout a concentration range of 1.0 to 300.0 µM. 0.4 µM was the limit of detection (LOD) attained using the DPV technique. The researchers successfully tested the Fe3O4/SPCE sensor for CTC detection in a real sample which resulted in recovery rates between 96.0% and 102.0%.

title: Application of a modified graphite screen-printed electrode for sensitive detection of vitamin C
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: Vitamin C, is a water-soluble vitamin that is found in varying amounts in a wide variety of fruits and vegetables. It is widely used in the food, chemical, and pharmaceutical industries. In this study, a quick, easy, affordable, and efficient electrochemical method was developed for detecting vitamin C. The electrochemical signal of vitamin C was significantly increased at the La2O3/Co3O4 nanocomposite-modified graphite screen-printed electrode (La2O3/Co3O4/GSPE). SEM, or scanning electron microscopy, was used to clarify the surface characterization clearer. Using differential pulse voltammetry, the limit of detection was determined to be 0.2 ± 0.01 µM with a good regression between the concentration and peak current of vitamin C (R2=0.9993) within the range of 0.7 to 450.0 µM. The modified electrode was effectively used to accurately measure vitamin C in actual samples.

title: A Novel Ni(II) nano-complex with schiff base ligand: Synthesis, spectroscopic characterization and study of antibacterial properties
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: A new mononuclear Ni(II) nanocomplex with the formula [Ni(L)2] (a) (L = 2-hydroxy-1-naphthaldehyde-2-aminothiophenol) has been synthesized by a sonochemical process. The nanocomplex (a) was characterized using FT-IR, UV-Vis, elemental analysis, single-crystal X-ray diffraction and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The average size of the nanocomplex synthesized via the sonochemical method was approximately 52 nm. Spectroscopic analyses revealed that the two Schiff base ligands form an octahedral geometry through the oxygen, sulfur and nitrogen atoms. The antibacterial behavior of the synthesized compound was investigated for two groups of gram-positive members of Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus ATCC 25923) and Enterococcus faecalis (Enter_faeca ATCC 29212) and two gram-negative members of Escherichia coli (E. coli ATCC 25922) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853). In this study, the inhibition method and the dilution method were used to determine the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and the minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC), and the results showed that the synthesized complex is active against bacteria.

title: Rational design of CNT-based nanocarriers for cancer therapy: An atomistic perspective on doxorubicin loading with –COOH and –OH groups
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX) is a potent chemotherapeutic agent with broad efficacy against various malignancies; however, its clinical use is restricted by dose-dependent cardiotoxicity and other systemic side effects. Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) have emerged as promising nanocarriers due to their high surface area, tunable surface chemistry, and potential to improve drug delivery efficiency. In this study, the adsorption and stabilization of DOX onto CNTs functionalized with –COOH and –OH groups were systematically examined using all-atom molecular dynamics simulations. Structural and energetic analyses—including potential and total energies, RMSD, contact number, center-of-mass distance, hydrogen bonding, non-bonded interaction energies, radius of gyration (Rg), solvent accessible surface area (SASA), and radial distribution function (RDF)—confirmed the structural stability and energetic consistency of the CNT–DOX complex under physiological conditions. Van der Waals forces were found to dominate the binding process, complemented by electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding interactions that enhance drug retention. The decrease in Rg and SASA indicated the formation of a compact and solvent-shielded structure, while RDF analysis showed preferential localization of DOX within ~1.0 nm of the CNT surface. These findings reveal the superior loading capacity and stability of functionalized CNTs and provide atomistic insights into their potential as efficient, biocompatible nanocarriers for targeted anticancer drug delivery.

title: Voltammetric determination of sulfanilamide as a medicinal drug using Fe3O4@CuO-RGO modified screen printed electrode
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: Sulfonamides (Such as sulfanilamide) are a kind of broad-spectrum antimicrobial drugs, used in livestock, poultry and aquaculture. Their residues in food may cause potential harm to consumers' health. Therefore, it is necessary to develop a simple, rapid and high-sensitivity detection method. In this investigation, graphite oxide (GO) was synthesized via a modified Hummer’s method to ensure enhanced oxidation efficiency. Iron oxide (Fe₃O₄) nanoparticles were prepared through a co-precipitation technique, followed by the fabrication of the Fe₃O₄@CuO-reduced graphene oxide (RGO) composite via a solvothermal procedure. Comprehensive characterization of the synthesized materials was conducted employing Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray Diffraction (XRD), Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy coupled with Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (FE-SEM/EDX), and Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM). These analyses confirmed the successful synthesis of the composite and provided substantive evidence of the proposed core-shell architecture of Fe₃O₄@CuO, highlighting its structural integrity and morphological features. Then, an electrochemical sensing method for detecting sulfonamide was established. Firstly, bare and modified electrode were screened using cyclic voltammetry(CV). The results showed that sulfonamide on magnetite (Fe3O4) @ CuO nanomaterials (CuO) - Reduced Graphene oxide (RGO) modified electrode had the largest response. The linear regression equation for modified electrode was y=0.352x+0.3753 (R2=0.9995) with the detection limit 0.03 µM. In this study, an electrode modification material with high sensitivity to sulfonamide was selected, and a simple, rapid and stable electrochemical detection method was established. This method has good applicability for determining sulfonamide drug residues in urine sample.

title: Reduced graphene oxide/ZnS nanowires modified screen printed electrode for the quantification of medicinal drug calcium folinate in injection samples
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: The research reports the development of a new type of modified screen-printed electrode (SPE) incorporating reduced graphene oxide and ZnS nanowires (rGO/ZnS NWs) for highly sensitive electrochemical detection of calcium folinate (CF). The behavior of the rGO/ZnS NWs-based SPE was investigated using cyclic voltammetry (CV), chronoamperometry, and differential pulse voltammetry (DPV). Relative to the bare SPE, the modi-fied electrode demonstrated markedly enhanced electrocatalytic proper-ties and a larger electroactive surface. Under optimized conditions, the rGO/ZnS NWs/SPE provided a wide linear response range (0.2–350.0 μM) along with a very low limit of detection (LOD=0.06 μM). In addition, it successfully measured calcium folinate in injection samples, yielding excellent recovery values (97.8–103.3%). Overall, the results highlight the suitability of the rGO/ZnS NWs-modified SPE as a fast, economical, and dependable tool for electroanalytical applications in pharmaceutical analysis.

title: Electrocatalytic oxidation of medicinal drug sertraline at a graphitic carbon nitride nanosheets and Zn-Co zeolitic imidazolate framework modified glassy carbon electrode
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: As a novel electrochemical platform for sertraline detection, a glassy carbon electrode modified with graphitic carbon nitride nanosheets (g-C3N4) and Zn-Co zeolitic imidazolate framework (Zn-Co ZIF) (g-C3N4/Zn-Co ZIF/GCE) is suggested. Using cyclic voltammetry (CV) studies in 0.1 M phosphate buffer solution (PBS), the electrochemical activity of g-C3N4/Zn-Co ZIF/GCE toward sertraline was examined. At g-C3N4/Zn-Co ZIF/GCE, sertraline's oxidation peak currents sharply increased and its overpotential considerably dropped. By employing differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) to analytically determine the concentration of sertraline, the potential utility of the sensor was shown. These findings are useful for actual sample analysis. The g-C3N4/Zn-Co ZIF/GCE had a detection limit of 0.3±0.01 μM utilizing DPV and operated linearly in the range of 1.0-385.0 μM. Sertraline was effectively detected in actual samples using the manufactured sensor. The tests showed that Zn-Co ZIF and g-C3N4 are suitable electrode materials that increase sensitivity and provide a high surface-to-volume ratio. Here, a novel sensor for measuring sertraline is presented that is easy to use, quick, sensitive, and economical.

title: Applications of chemically modified electrodes in norepinephrine analysis: A review
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: Norepinephrine (NEP) is classified as a catecholamine, a neurotransmitter that is essential to human function. Catecholamines in biological samples must be measured precisely and selectively to be used for clinical diagnosis and the study of certain pathological disorders. Modification of the working electrode surface is often employed to achieve rapid, accurate, selective, and sensitive detection of NEP quickly, accurately, selectively, and sensitively. Several research approaches that have effectively identified NEP utilizing surface-modified electrodes in various genuine samples have been carefully reviewed in this work. With a variety of modified electrodes, such as glassy carbon, carbon paste, screen-printed electrodes, and those augmented with carbon nanotubes (CNTs), the electrochemical detection of NEP is the main focus. The analytical performance indicators of several research methodologies for NEP detection are also covered.

title: A review of recent advances in the application of MXene-modified electrochemical sensors for the detection of specific drugs
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: The remarkable qualities of MXene, a new family of two-dimensional transition metal carbides, such as its hydrophilicity, high electrical conductivity, huge surface area, and attractive topological structure, have made it a potential material for a number of uses. MXenes are efficient transducers for electrochemical sensing because they can dissolve in ordinary solvents and combine with other nanomaterials to produce composites. According to the literature, MXenes are increasingly being used in the detection of various analytes. An overview of the applications of MXene-modified materials is provided for sensing applications in this study. The analytes are grouped, and a thorough explanation of each category is provided to facilitate the audience’s understanding.

title: Nanocarriers in medicine: A review of current advances and clinical applications
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: It's becoming increasingly clear that nanocarriers are fundamentally changing how we approach modern medicine. By allowing for incredibly precise drug delivery, they're making treatments more effective while dramatically reducing those dreaded side effects. These sophisticated tiny systems, which operate on the scale of 1 to 1000 nanometers, work by encapsulating therapeutic compounds. This shields them from breaking down too early, improves their solubility, and lets doctors control exactly when and where they're released. This review takes a deep dive into the different types of nanocarriers out there, from organic to inorganic and even hybrid materials, and explores how they're being used to fight cancer, infections, and to aid in tissue regeneration and diagnostics. We also tackle the big hurdles—like making sure they're biocompatible, figuring out how to manufacture them at scale, and navigating the regulatory maze—while also spotlighting the coolest new advances, like stimuli-responsive carriers and designs that mimic our body's own extracellular matrix. Finally, we'll look at what the future might hold, including wider clinical use and truly personalized nanomedicine.

title: Bisphenol a: Analysis using modified graphite screen printed electrode as an electrochemical sensor
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: The La2O3/Co3O4 nanocomposite modified graphite screen printed electrode (La2O3/Co3O4/GSPE) was used to create an electrochemical sensor for the electrochemical measurement of bisphenol A. Through the use of SEM, the La2O3/Co3O4 nanocomposite was characterized. Voltammetry was employed to study the electrochemical properties of bisphenol A. The electrode modification caused a notable shift in the peak potential (~220 mV) and a significant rise in the anodic peak current (~2.5 times). The oxidation peak current of bisphenol A fluctuated linearly with concentration under ideal circumstances, spanning a broad range of 0.5 to 450.0 µM. The detection limit of this technique was as low as 0.15 µM. The proposed technique was also successfully applied to identify bisphenol A in actual samples.

title: Functionalized graphene enhances irinotecan binding: An all-atom MD study of –OH/–COOH decorated surfaces
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: The development of efficient nanocarriers for anticancer therapeutics remains a major challenge due to limitations in drug solubility, bioavailability, and systemic toxicity. In this work, all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were employed to investigate the adsorption behavior of the chemotherapeutic agent irinotecan on pristine graphene (GRP) and functionalized graphene (GRP-F) decorated with hydroxyl (–OH) and carboxyl (–COOH) groups. Both systems were simulated for 100 ns under explicit solvent conditions using the CHARMM36 force field. Energy analyses revealed that drug binding to pristine graphene was predominantly driven by van der Waals interactions, whereas the functionalized surface provided additional stabilization through electrostatic interactions and intermittent hydrogen bonding. Root mean square deviation (RMSD) and radius of gyration (Rg) analyses confirmed the stable adsorption of irinotecan on both carriers, with reduced conformational fluctuations in the GRP-F complex. Contact number and center-of-mass distance profiles demonstrated tighter and more persistent drug–carrier associations in the functionalized system. Moreover, solvent accessible surface area (SASA) analysis indicated reduced solvent exposure upon adsorption, while radial distribution functions (RDF) highlighted a significantly higher probability density of irinotecan near GRP-F compared with pristine graphene. Overall, these findings demonstrate that surface functionalization enhances the binding affinity and stability of irinotecan adsorption on graphene, providing a more favorable platform for drug loading and retention. This study offers atomistic-level insights into graphene-based nanocarriers and underscores the potential of functionalized graphene for the design of next-generation delivery systems for chemotherapeutic agents.

title: Bimetallic nanoparticle of yttrium-copper metal-organic framework (Y-Cu-MOF) as a novel modifier for determination of ascorbic acid
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: A solvothermal synthesis approach was used to fabricate a bimetallic metal-organic framework (MOF) based on yttrium and copper (Y-Cu MOF). The formed material was characterized extensively using several techniques including field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and elemental mapping. Subsequently, a voltammetric platform for the selective detection of ascorbic acid (ASA) was generated from the Y-Cu MOF nanostructure by modifying a screen-printed electrode (SPE) (Y-Cu-MOFs/SPE). A detailed electrochemical evaluation was also conducted using a wide range of electroanalytical techniques for the modified electrode and its response against ASA. The electrochemical results using the modified electrode demonstrated a large increase in current response associated with the oxidation of ASA, benefiting from the facilitating properties of the Y-Cu-MOFs. The Y-Cu-MOFs/CPE sensor also verified great sensitivity toward the detection of ASA within a linear detection range (0.4-500.0 μM) and a detection limit that was as low as 0.1±0.01 μM, when operated under the optimized conditions. The obtained results also verified practical analysis with recovery rates of ASA ranging from 97.1% to 102.0%. on the Y-Cu-MOFs/CPE electrochemical sensor in both the ASA injection samples and urine.

title: Killing of breast cancer cells by nano-coated graphene oxide: targeting with folic acid and loading with carvacrol
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: In this investigation, we developed a graphene oxide (GO) based biocompatible and targeted nanobiocomposite using folic acid (FA) and human serum albumin (HSA) that carvacrol is loaded on graphene sheets. Separately, GO was conjugated to poly l-lysine (PLL) (GO-PLL) and HSA was conjugated to FA (HSA-FA). Then GO-PLL was covalently linked to HSA-FA. SEM showed that GO-PLL sheets were nano-coated by HSA-FA layer (HSA-FA nano-coated GO-PLL). HSA-FA nano-coated GO-PLL was applied for modification of glassy carbon electrode surface. The modified electrode was used for study of MCF7 cancer cells using linear sweep voltammetry method. Results showed a decrease in signal of conjugated folic acid concurrently with increasing the number of MCF7 cells. So, carvacrol was loaded on nano-coated GO-PLL sheets by π-π interactions. Entrapment efficiency (EE%) of carvacrol was 90.8 %. Cytotoxicity effect of carvacrol-loaded nano-coated GO-PLL was evaluated on MCF-7 cell line using the 3-[4,5 dimethylthiazol-2-yl]-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide (MTT) test. The cells were exposed to the free carvacrol, GO, unloaded-nanobiocomposite, and carvacrol-loaded nano-coated GO-PLL for 48 h. The IC50 of free carvacrol and the carvacrol-loaded nano-coated GO-PLL were determined to be 0.8 mg/ml and 1 mg/ml, respectively. The findings of this study demonstrated the potential of the as-prepared GO-based nanobiocomposite in inducing cytotoxicity against breast cancer cells.

title: Preparation of bimetallic Cu, Zn complex with OPD: Synthesis, characterization, spectroscopic methods, and interaction with FS-DNA
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: In this study, the bimetallic [Zn(OPD)(μ-SCN)Cu(OPD)] (a), where OPD = o-phenylenediamine ligand, was synthesized. The complex (a) was studied by spectral tools, such as FT-IR and UV-Vis spectroscopy. Interaction studies of complex (a) with fish sperm DNA (FS-DNA) were also conducted using fluorescence, UV-Vis, and gel electrophoresis techniques. Additionally, thermodynamic parameters ΔH°, ΔS°, and ΔG° were calculated from these interactions. The results revealed the hydrogen bonding and van der Waals forces in groove binding mode interaction between the complex (a) and the DNA. Noteworthy, the viscosity measurement showed that increased concentration of the complex has no effect on DNA viscosity, suggesting that binding interaction will not produce much distortion of the helical structure of the DNA. Circular dichroism (CD) spectra revealed extensive alteration in the DNA structure upon interaction of the DNA with the complex (a). This means that while the complex unfolds the DNA in coordination without changing its viscosity, it decreases detectable conformational changes by CD spectroscopy. This discovery in two ways illustrates how complex stealthily manipulates DNA structure and indicates the significance of using more than a single analytical method to efficiently distinguish between metal-DNA interactions.

title: Theoretical investigation of C20 nanocarrier for fluoxetine in biological media
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: Recently, fullerene nanoparticles have garnered significant interest because of their distinct physical and chemical characteristics. When appropriately modified, these nanoparticles exhibit strong biocompatibility, notable anti-tumor effects, and anti-depressant properties, making them promising for cancer and depression treatment. In this study, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were employed to theoretically analyze the interaction between fluoxetine (F), a medicinal compound, and the C20 surface in both gas phase and physiological environments. The DFT results and adsorption energy data indicate that this nanocarrier performs effectively in biological systems.

title: Electrochemical determination of methyldopa using modified screen printed carbon electrode
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: This study aimed to design and build an electrochemical sensing platform for measuring methyldopa (MDP). To do this, a nanocomposite of CoWO4 nanoparticles (NPs) anchored to reduced grapheme oxide nanosheets (rGO NSs) was made using a straightforward hydrothermal method. FE-SEM techniques were employed to verify the synthesis of the CoWO4/rGO nanocomposite (CWRGs). The produced CWRGs were then used to modify the surface of a screen-printed carbon electrode (SPCE) to enhance MDP determination. The outstanding electrochemical response of the modified SPCE (CWRGs/SPCE) to the MDP oxidation was investigated using cyclic voltammetry (CV) due to the advantageous properties of CoWO4 NPs and rGO NSs as well as their complimentary effects. For MDP determination, the CWRGs/SPCE sensor showed a low limit of detection (LOD) of 0.1±0.01 μM and a wide linear detection range of 0.3 to 180.0 μM under ideal circumstances. Additionally, CWRGs/SPCE had a sensitivity of 0.1156 μA/μM for MDP detection. Furthermore, the possibility for detecting this molecule in actual samples was demonstrated by the excellent recoveries for detecting spiked MDP in the MDP tablet and urine samples at the CWRGs/SPCE surface.

title: Carbon nanomaterials-modified electrochemical sensors and their applications in the detection of vitamins B, C, D, and K
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: Vitamins are a class of organic substances that are essential to the proper functioning of living organisms. Certain vitamins are considered important because, although they can be produced by these organisms, they must be consumed to meet their needs. The human body may develop metabolic diseases as a result of vitamin deficiencies or insufficiencies; therefore, it is critical to monitor vitamin levels and ensure you get enough of them daily through food or supplements. The determination of vitamins is primarily achieved through various analytical methods, including chromatographic, spectroscopic, and spectrometric techniques. Ongoing research aims to develop new and more efficient methodologies for vitamin analysis, with electroanalytical methods, particularly voltammetry, being among the most common. This study focuses on the use of electroanalytical techniques for vitamin determination, highlighting the advancements in voltammetry developed in recent years. Specifically, this review provides a comprehensive bibliographic survey of modified electrode surfaces utilizing carbon nanomaterials for vitamin analysis.

title: Removal of methylene blue from water samples using multi-walled carbon nanotube/ ZnCo-zeolite imidazole framework nanocomposite
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: The ZnCo-Zeolite imidazole framework multi-walled carbon nanotube nanocomposite was prepared for the study. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffractometry (XRD), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) were used in the characterization of the synthesized nanocomposite. The catalytic performance of the nanocomposite was also examined for its probable adsorptive removal of methylene blue (MB). Experiments were also conducted on the influence of different parameters such as ionic strength, pH, contact time, and initial concentration. Freundlich and Langmuir isotherms were employed to fit the adsorption equilibrium data, and the Langmuir model was the most appropriate. For the MB removal, the maximum sorption capacity was found to be 28.57 mg/g at 298 K. Both pseudo-first order and pseudo-second order diffusion models were employed to determine the adsorption kinetics and the best one was the pseudo-first order model. The as-prepared nanocomposite has high adsorption capacity for MB from water samples based on these data.

title: Molecular dynamics-informed design of functionalized graphene oxide nanocarriers for enhanced romidepsin delivery in solid tumor therapy
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: Romidepsin (ROM) is a cyclic peptide and FDA-approved histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor with strong antitumor activity in hematological malignancies. However, its clinical application in solid tumors is limited due to poor aqueous solubility, rapid systemic clearance, and unfavorable bio-distribution. We performed 200-nanosecond all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations under physiologically relevant conditions to investigate the ROM interaction with a hydroxyl- and carboxyl-functionalized graphene oxide (GRP) nanosheet. The system was analyzed using metrics including root mean square deviation (RMSD), interaction energy decomposition, hydrogen bonding, and solvent-accessible surface area (SASA). ROM exhibited rapid and stable adsorption onto the GRP surface, primarily driven by van der Waals and π–π stacking interactions, with further stabilization via hydrogen bonding. ROM molecules formed stable, multilayered aggregates on GRP without significant structural disruption, maintaining close surface contact throughout the trajectory. SASA analysis showed increased aqueous exposure and dispersibility of the ROM–GRP complex relative to GRP alone. The results demonstrate the high-affinity, stable loading of ROM onto functionalized GRP, providing atomistic insights into the encapsulation and solubilization mechanism. These findings provide a theoretical framework for the development of GRP-based nanocarriers to improve ROM delivery in solid tumor therapy and support further in vitro and in vivo validation of this nanoplatform for biomedical applications.

title: Swcnt-based nanocarriers for improved pharmacokinetics of omacetaxine mepesuccinate in hematological malignancies
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) is a myeloproliferative neoplasm driven by the BCR-ABL1 fusion oncogene, for which tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) have significantly improved patient outcomes. However, the emergence of TKI resistance and the pharmacological limitations of alternative agents such as omacetaxine mepesuccinate—namely, poor solubility, rapid metabolism, and dose-limiting toxicities—underscore the need for advanced drug delivery strategies. This study investigates the encapsulation dynamics and molecular interactions of omacetaxine mepesuccinate within single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) as a potential nanocarrier platform, using state-of-the-art molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. A capped, armchair SWCNT (4.0 nm length, 1.3 nm diameter) and an optimized omacetaxine molecule were constructed and parameterized using the CHARMM36 force field. The SWCNT/omacetaxine complex was simulated in explicit aqueous solution under physiological conditions for 200 ns using GROMACS 2024.5. Analyses included assessments of system stability, drug encapsulation efficiency, interaction energy profiles, conformational dynamics, and solvent accessibility. MD simulations revealed spontaneous encapsulation and persistent confinement of omacetaxine within the SWCNT cavity, driven predominantly by strong van der Waals and π–π interactions, with negligible electrostatic contributions. The complex exhibited remarkable structural and energetic stability, as evidenced by stable potential energy, Root Mean Square Deviation, and radius of gyration values throughout the simulation.

title: Fe₃O₄-NH₂/GO an effective modifier for simultaneous voltammetric detection of isoniazid in the presence of acetaminophen
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: This study describes a simple and cost-effective procedure to develop a new electrochemical sensor to simultaneously detect acetaminophen (AC) and isoniazid (INZ). We present the study of a screen-printed graphite electrode (SPGE) modified with Fe3O4-NH2/GO nanocomposite by differential pulse voltammetry (DPV), chronoamperometry (CHA), and cyclic voltammetry (CV). Additionally, we used X-ray diffraction (XRD), vibrating sample magnetometry (VSM), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), and field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) to characterize the synthesized nanocomposites. The DPV peak current of INZ increases linearly with a concentration in the range 0.07-460.0 µM and its limit of detection (LOD) is 0.02±0.001 µM. The results show that the modified electrode exhibits robust functions to circumvent the problem of overlapping the two voltammetric peaks of INZ and AC. We demonstrate the interest in using Fe3O4-NH2/GO/SPGE to detect INZ and AC in real samples.

title: MOF/MWCNTs nanocomposite modified glassy carbon electrode for voltammetric determination of sulfanilamide
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: Sulfanilamide (SFA) is a synthetic antimicrobial chemical that belongs to the sulfonamides class and is frequently used for both therapeutic and preventative purposes in both human and veterinary medicine. The solvothermal method was used in this study to successfully prepare a nanocomposite material of an iron-based metal-organic framework (MIL-101(Fe)-NH₂) with the addition of multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs), or MIL-101(Fe)-NH₂/MWCNTs. The prepared nanocomposite was then utilized as the working electrode for the voltammetric determination of SFA after modifying a glassy carbon electrode (GCE) to create the MIL-101(Fe)-NH₂/MWCNTs/GCE. The modified electrode demonstrated notable electrocatalytic activity towards the SFA oxidation compared to the bare GCE. Under optimized experimental conditions, the oxidation peak current of SFA increased linearly with concentration between 0.5 and 100.0 μM, with a computed limit of detection of 0.3±0.02 μM.

title: Synthesis of MoO₃ nanoparticles and its application to construct an electrochemical sensor for determination of hydroxylamine
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: In this study, MoO3 nanoparticles (MoO3 NPs) were fabricated through a straightforward technique. Confirmation of their formation was provided by FT-IR, XRD, FE-SEM, and EDX. Subsequently, an electronic sensing device, which incorporated a pre-designed graphite-based electrode (SPGE) combined with MoO3 NPs, was introduced for the analysis of hydroxylamine presence in aqueous solutions. The combined MoO3 NPs and SPGE setup exhibited remarkable efficacy in detecting hydroxylamine, a phenomenon supported by cyclic voltammetry (CV) data. A unique oxidation signature without a corresponding reduction in the reverse scan was observed, revealing the one-way nature of hydroxylamine's electrochemical oxidation on both the standard SPGE and the combined MoO3/SPGE setup. When conditions were optimized (pH and pulsing specifics), a consistent correlation with its concentration, spanning from 0.04 µM to 675.0 µM and having a sensitivity threshold (LOD) of 0.01 µM, was exhibited by the voltammetric reaction of hydroxylamine on the MoO3/SPGE. Moreover, the real-world relevance of the MoO3/SPGE sensing apparatus was assessed by measuring hydroxylamine levels in water sources. Data highlighted recuperation metrics from 96.7% to 104.3% and consistency measures (RSDs) at or less than 3.1% for both river and domestic water specimens.

title: Antibacterial effects of mixed ligand complex formation of 2-Aminobenzamide with Cu(II) in the presence of glycine
journal: Advanced Journal of Nanochemistry and Medicine
abstract: A mixed ligand of bioactive Cu(II) complex has been synthesized from 2aminobenzamide (2AB) and glycine (gly). Then structurally characterized by various physico-chemical and spectral studies such as FT-IR, UV- Vis methods and elemental analysis. The results showed that the 2-aminobenzamide ligand was coordinated to the metal ion via the N and O atoms. Based on the spectral studies, both the ligands act as bidentates and they chelate with Cu(II) ion to form a stable six, five membered chelate ring with octahedral geometry. In this study, inhibition method and dilution method were used to determine the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and the lowest bactericidal concentration (MBC) and the results showed that the synthesized complex against bacteria are active. The antibacterial behavior of the synthesized compound was examined for two groups of gram-negative bacteria (Escherichia coli) and gram-positive (Staphylococus aureus). The results showed that among the synthesized samples complex showed higher antimicrobial activity than ligands.
